fact: The A80 Supra's 2JZ-GTE engine became legendary for its ability to handle over 1,000hp with minimal modifications — making it one of the most tuned engines in history.
The 993 was the last air-cooled 911 Porsche ever made — widely considered by enthusiasts to be the purest and most beautiful 911 of all time.
The FD RX-7 is one of the lightest sports cars of its era, and the only mass-production car of the 1990s powered by a twin-turbocharged rotary engine.
The Testarossa's iconic side strakes weren't just styling — they channelled air to the massive side-mounted radiators needed to cool its wide flat-12 engine.
The original Mustang sold over 1 million units in its first 18 months — a record that had never been seen in the automotive industry before.
The Countach's scissor doors and wedge shape were so radical that the word 'countach' — a Piedmontese exclamation of astonishment — became its name after designer Gandini first sketched it.
The R34 GT-R was officially rated at 280hp due to a gentlemen's agreement between Japanese manufacturers — but independent tests consistently showed it producing closer to 330hp.
The E30 M3 was built primarily to go racing — BMW needed to homologate it for touring car competitions, which is why it has a completely different engine from the standard 3 Series.
At just 725kg, the Lotus Elise weighs less than half of most modern SUVs — and its revolutionary bonded aluminium chassis was so innovative it influenced how sports cars are built to this day.
The original Viper had no roof, no side windows, no ABS, no traction control, and no airbags — Dodge intentionally built it as a raw, dangerous driving experience.
